================================================================================
USER-KING REVIEWER DIRECTIVES - SUPREME AUTHORITY (CLAUDE.md §3c)
Source: Human SME review of Automotive v1,
"Feedback: Automotive Lakehouse Data Models - Value Chain Coverage Review",
linked from the "Active Vibe Models Enriched" tracking sheet (Reviewer Notes).
These reviewer requirements OUTRANK every heuristic, score, and LLM opinion.
Apply ALL of them to the ECM (and carry them through to the MVM on shrink).
Where a directive conflicts with an agent auto-priority below, the REVIEWER WINS.
The reviewer's #1 finding: Field Services is the weakest value-chain area (no
dedicated domain); secondary gaps are Sales F&I, digital sales, ESG/sustainability,
simulation R&D data, an explicit OEE view, connected-vehicle-to-aftersales
integration, and thin Procurement/Mobility coverage in the MVM.
================================================================================

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 1 - add_domain field_services: the value chain has NO dedicated Field Services domain and this is the single biggest gap (Field Services rated WEAK). Add a field_services domain in the operations division. Create the field_services domain with the following products: field_technician_dispatch, mobile_service_order, roadside_assistance_case, towing_event, breakdown_case, field_visit, field_activity, field_quality_investigation, field_failure_analysis, field_engineering_report, field_service_appointment, field_parts_usage.
Add more tables to the field_services domain to cover field technician dispatching, mobile service orders, roadside assistance and towing, breakdown management, OEM field-representative visit and activity tracking, field quality investigations, field failure analysis, and field engineering reports.
Rationale: field-service concepts are currently scattered across aftersales, dealer, and mobility with no cohesive structure; consolidate them into a first-class domain.

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 2 - add F&I products to sales: Financing and leasing (F&I - Finance & Insurance) is a major revenue stream that is NOT modeled and is a notable Sales gap. Add more tables to the sales domain to cover Finance & Insurance (F&I): finance_contract, lease_contract, insurance_policy, fni_menu_product, credit_application, residual_value_schedule.
Rationale: F&I (financing, leasing, insurance) is a core OEM/dealer revenue stream missing from the sales flow.

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 3 - add digital and direct sales products to sales: Online/digital sales channels are absent, increasingly important as OEMs move to agency/direct models. Add more tables to the sales domain to cover digital and direct-to-consumer sales: configurator_session, online_order, ecommerce_cart, digital_sales_lead, vehicle_subscription.
Rationale: configurator sessions, online orders, e-commerce, and subscription (vehicle-as-a-service) must connect to the sales flow.

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 4 - add simulation and requirements R&D products to engineering: advanced R&D lacks dedicated data products for simulation-result data and requirements traceability. Add more tables to the engineering domain for simulation data management and requirements: cfd_simulation_result, fea_simulation_result, nvh_test_result, test_bench_run, sensor_dataset, driving_scenario_library, requirements_traceability.
Rationale: CFD/FEA/NVH result datasets, test-bench data, autonomous-driving sensor/scenario datasets, and DOORS/Polarion/Jira requirements traceability strengthen R&D.

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 5 - add ESG and energy products (production + governance): ESG / sustainability data is underrepresented and increasingly mandatory (CSRD, EU Taxonomy). Add more tables to the manufacturing domain for ESG and energy tracking: energy_consumption_record, co2_emission_record, water_usage_record, line_energy_meter.
Add more tables to the compliance domain for ESG reporting: esg_report, social_compliance_audit, sustainability_metric.
Rationale: CO2 emissions, per-line/plant energy and water usage, social compliance audits, and ESG reporting structures are increasingly required and currently missing.

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 6 - add OEE products to manufacturing (metric-view alternative): OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) is only implicitly calculable; the reviewer asks for an explicit OEE metric view OR a pre-aggregated OEE data product. Add more tables to the manufacturing domain for Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE): oee_daily_snapshot, equipment_effectiveness_metric.
Rationale: a pre-aggregated OEE product (availability x performance x quality from downtime_event and production_confirmation) makes OEE analytics-ready.

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 7 - connect connected-vehicle telemetry to aftersales service (cross-domain workflow): integration between connected-vehicle telemetry and service scheduling (proactive maintenance triggers) is not modeled. In the aftersales domain, the service appointment / service order table should reference mobility.connected_vehicle: add column connected_vehicle_id to the aftersales service appointment table with FK to mobility.connected_vehicle. Also add column service_order_id to mobility.predictive_maintenance_alert with FK to the aftersales service order table so predictive-maintenance alerts flow into aftersales service scheduling.
Rationale: connected-vehicle DTC/telemetry and predictive-maintenance alerts must trigger aftersales service (proactive maintenance), bridging mobility and aftersales.

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 8 - strengthen Procurement and Mobility in the MVM: the MVM excludes Procurement and Mobility entirely, which is too aggressive; basic purchasing and connected-vehicle data are increasingly core. When shrinking the ECM to the MVM, keep basic Procurement in the MVM: purchase_order, purchase_order_line, purchase_requisition, supplier, scheduling_agreement, goods_receipt. Also keep the Mobility basics in the MVM: connected_vehicle, telemetry_event, predictive_maintenance_alert.
Rationale: excluding Procurement and Mobility from the MVM leaves small-to-mid operations without basic purchasing and connected-vehicle coverage.

REVIEWER-PRESERVE (do NOT regress these - the reviewer explicitly called them strong, and §3b protects every existing domain name verbatim):
  - PROTECTED DOMAINS (keep verbatim, never rename/remove/merge): vehicle, product, engineering, manufacturing, supply, procurement, quality, logistics, inventory, asset, customer, sales, dealer, aftersales, billing, mobility, finance, workforce, compliance - and the newly added field_services.
  - R&D (engineering, vehicle): keep engineering BOMs, design specs, CAD refs, DVP, FMEA, ECU/powertrain/material specs, ECO/ECN, program milestones (P0..SOP), prototype/validation, digital twins.
  - Purchasing (procurement, supply): keep contract governance, PO/requisitions/sourcing, spend analytics, supplier scorecards, PPAP, RFQ, scheduling agreements (JIT/JIS).
  - Production (manufacturing, quality, inventory): keep production orders/build sequences, mBOM/routing, downtime/shopfloor events, WIP; keep the IATF 16949/APQP toolkit (FMEA, control plans, SPC, PPAP, defects, audits).
  - Logistics: keep finished-vehicle logistics (compounds, movements, handovers, transport orders, vessel voyages, load plans) and multi-modal transport.
  - Sales/Dealer/Customer: keep the franchise dealer model, fleet contracts, incentive programs, MSRP scheduling, configurator-to-order traceability, loyalty and ownership.
  - Aftersales: keep the strong warranty (policies/claims/goodwill/returns), recall (campaigns/VINs/completions), TSBs, parts distribution, labor-time standards.
  - Keep all dbx_pii_* PII classification tags (useful for masking and access control).
  - Keep the ECM/MVM scope split and the 3-division taxonomy (operations/business/corporate); do not add a 4th division.

SAE automation level for the ADAS (Advanced Driver Assistance Systems) features included in this homologation variant, ranging from Level 0 (no automation) to Level 5 (full automation).
Reference to the specific trim level or configuration within the nameplate that this homologation variant applies to. Nullable if variant applies to all trims.
Name of the government agency, regulatory body, or authorized technical service that issued the homologation approval. Examples include NHTSA, EPA, CARB, TÜV, or national transport ministries.
Date on which the regulatory authority officially granted homologation approval for this variant. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
Official approval or certification number issued by the regulatory authority upon successful homologation. This number is typically required for vehicle registration and sales in the target market.
Indicates whether this homologation variant requires changes to the base SKU Bill of Materials. True if BOM modifications are needed, False if only calibration or documentation changes are required.
Indicates whether this homologation variant is certified for CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) compliance in the United States market. Applicable to US market variants only.
Additional notes, comments, or special instructions related to regulatory compliance, testing requirements, or market-specific considerations for this homologation variant.

Incremental cost associated with implementing this homologation variant compared to the base SKU, including parts, labor, testing, and certification fees. Expressed in the currency specified in cost_delta_currency.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the cost_delta_amount field.
Timestamp when this homologation variant record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Date from which this homologation variant becomes valid and vehicles can be legally sold or registered in the target market. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
Specific emissions standard or tier that this homologation variant is designed to meet, such as Euro 6d, EPA Tier 3, CARB LEV III, or China 6b.
Date on which this homologation approval expires or becomes invalid, requiring renewal or re-certification. Nullable for approvals without expiration. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
Unique identifier for the homologation variant record. Primary key.
Timestamp when this homologation variant record was last updated or modified. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Typical lead time in days required to obtain homologation approval for this variant from the date of submission to the regulatory authority.
Model year designation for which this homologation variant is applicable. Aligns with the automotive industry model year convention.

Detailed description of the technical modifications, component changes, or configuration adjustments required to meet the target market regulatory requirements. May reference specific parts, calibrations, or design changes.

High-level classification of the type of modification required for homologation compliance, such as hardware changes, software updates, calibration adjustments, documentation updates, labeling changes, or additional testing.

Safety rating achieved by this homologation variant under the applicable NCAP (New Car Assessment Programme) testing protocol, such as Euro NCAP, US NCAP, or ANCAP. Typically expressed as a star rating or score.

Indicates whether this homologation variant includes OTA (Over-the-Air) update capability for software and firmware updates. Relevant for regulatory compliance with evolving software update requirements.

Type of powertrain for which this homologation variant is certified. ICE (Internal Combustion Engine), HEV (Hybrid Electric Vehicle), PHEV (Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle), BEV (Battery Electric Vehicle), FCEV (Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle).
Reference to the vehicle nameplate (model line) that this homologation variant applies to. Links to the nameplate master data.

Classification of the primary regulatory domain this variant addresses, such as safety standards, emissions controls, environmental compliance, or fuel economy requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Safety|Emissions|Environmental|Fuel Economy|Crash Test|Lighting|Braking|Occupant Protection — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Primary regulatory standard or framework that this homologation variant must comply with. Examples include UNECE (United Nations Economic Commission for Europe), FMVSS (Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards), ADR (Australian Design Rules), CARB (California Air Resources Board). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: UNECE|FMVSS|ADR|CARB|EPA|Euro NCAP|IATF 16949|ISO 14001 — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Indicates whether this homologation approval requires periodic renewal or re-certification. True if renewal is mandated by the regulatory authority, False if approval is perpetual or tied to model year.
Name of the engineer or technical specialist responsible for managing the homologation process and regulatory compliance for this variant.
Reference to the base commercial SKU that this homologation variant is derived from. Links to the product catalog SKU master.
Date on which the homologation application and supporting documentation were submitted to the regulatory authority for review. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country code representing the target market or jurisdiction for which this homologation variant is certified.
Broader geographic region classification for the target market, used for regional compliance grouping and reporting.

Reference number or identifier for the official test report(s) submitted as part of the homologation application. Links to laboratory test results, crash test data, emissions testing, or other certification evidence.
Name of the accredited testing laboratory or technical service that conducted the homologation testing and issued the test reports.
Unique alphanumeric code identifying this specific homologation variant within the product catalog. Used for internal tracking and cross-referencing with regulatory submissions.
Human-readable name or designation for this homologation variant, typically including market and regulatory standard identifiers.

Current lifecycle status of the homologation variant in the approval and production process. Tracks progression from initial submission through approval, active use, and eventual expiration or withdrawal. Indicates whether this homologation variant has been tested and certified under the WLTP (Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure) standard for fuel consumption and emissions.

after.description: Reference catalog of commercial body style definitions available across nameplates (e.g., 2-door coupe, 4-door sedan, crew cab pickup, extended cab, SUV 3-row, cargo van). Captures body style code, body style name, door count, seating capacity, cargo volume, roof type, body structure classification (unibody/body-on-frame), and applicable vehicle segment. Used in SKU construction, order management, and regulatory homologation classification.
Master reference table for market. Referenced by market_id.

SSOT for vehicle nameplate definitions — the commercial brand identity of a vehicle line (e.g., F-150, Silverado, Camry, Mustang). Owns nameplate code, brand affiliation, vehicle segment classification (car/truck/SUV/commercial), powertrain family (ICE/HEV/PHEV/EV), market positioning tier, global vs. regional availability flag, nameplate lifecycle status (active/discontinued), SOP (Start of Production) year, EOP (End of Production) year, and nameplate heritage lineage. This is the root anchor for all program and model year planning.

before.description: Defines the annual program plan for each nameplate by MY (Model Year). Captures MY designation, program code, program phase (concept/development/launch/production/runout), SOP date, EOP date, target plant assignments, planned production volume, regulatory homologation targets (CAFE, WLTP, EPA), program budget envelope (CapEx), and program manager reference. Acts as the planning backbone linking nameplate definitions to annual production and sales programs.

Defines commercially available option packages and standalone options that can be ordered on a vehicle (e.g., Technology Package, Tow Package, Panoramic Roof, Premium Audio). Captures package code, package name, package type (group/standalone/accessory), MSRP uplift price, content description, constraint rules (requires/excludes other packages), availability by trim level, market availability regions, and lifecycle status. Distinct from engineering feature definitions — this is the commercial catalog layer.

Defines the commercial trim hierarchy for a model year program (e.g., Base, XL, XLT, Lariat, Platinum, Limited). Captures trim code, trim name, trim rank/order within the nameplate hierarchy, standard feature set description, MSRP base price, market segment positioning, availability regions, and active/inactive lifecycle status. Trim levels are the primary commercial differentiation layer between the nameplate and individual option packages.

Reference catalog of commercial body style definitions available across nameplates (e.g., 2-door coupe, 4-door sedan, crew cab pickup, extended cab, SUV 3-row, cargo van). Captures body style code, body style name, door count, seating capacity, cargo volume, roof type, body structure classification (unibody/body-on-frame), and applicable vehicle segment. Used in SKU construction, order management, and regulatory homologation classification.

Commercial color catalog defining all available exterior paint colors and interior color/material combinations offered across model year programs. Captures color code, color name, color type (exterior/interior), color family, paint technology (solid/metallic/pearl/matte), interior material type (cloth/leather/synthetic/premium), availability by trim level, MSRP uplift (for premium colors), regional availability, and active/discontinued status. Used in SKU configuration, order management, and production scheduling.

Defines market-specific homologation variants of a base SKU required to meet local regulatory standards (UNECE, FMVSS, ADR, etc.). Captures homologation variant code, base SKU reference, target market/country, regulatory standard (UNECE/FMVSS/ADR/CARB), required modification description, homologation approval number, approval authority, approval date, expiry date, and variant status. Bridges the commercial product catalog to the compliance domain's regulatory approval records.
Master reference table for market. Referenced by market_id.

Defines the feature-to-market availability matrix — which SKUs, trim levels, and option packages are available in which geographic markets and sales channels. Captures market code, sales channel (retail/fleet/government/export), availability status (available/restricted/not-offered), launch date, withdrawal date, homologation approval status, import duty classification, and CKD/SKD (Completely Knocked Down / Semi Knocked Down) assembly flag. Critical for order management, dealer ordering systems, and regulatory compliance.

SSOT for MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) price books by model year, market, and currency. Captures price book code, effective date range, market/region code, currency code, price book status (draft/approved/published/superseded), approval authority, and publication date. The price book is the container for all MSRP pricing entries and governs which prices are active for dealer ordering and consumer-facing communications.

Individual MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) pricing entries within a price book. Captures the SKU or option package being priced, base MSRP amount, destination charge, gas guzzler tax (if applicable), effective start and end dates, price type (base vehicle/option/package/accessory), and prior price for change tracking. Enables dealer invoice generation, consumer window sticker production, and competitive pricing analysis.

SSOT for vehicle nameplate definitions — the commercial brand identity of a vehicle line (e.g., F-150, Silverado, Camry, Mustang). Owns nameplate code, brand affiliation, vehicle segment classification (car/truck/SUV/commercial), powertrain family (ICE/HEV/PHEV/EV), market positioning tier, global vs. regional availability flag, nameplate lifecycle status (active/discontinued), SOP (Start of Production) year, EOP (End of Production) year, and nameplate heritage lineage. This is the root anchor for all program and model year planning.

The formal dealer order guide defining which SKUs, trim levels, option packages, and colors are orderable by dealers for a given MY, market, and sales channel. Captures order guide version, effective date range, market/region, sales channel, orderable SKU list, option availability matrix, minimum/maximum order constraints, and order guide approval status. Published to dealer DMS systems and governs what dealers can order from the factory.

Commercial powertrain configuration catalog defining the orderable powertrain combinations available for each nameplate and MY. Captures powertrain code, engine displacement, cylinder count, fuel type (gasoline/diesel/hybrid/PHEV/BEV/FCEV), electric motor configuration (for EV/HEV/PHEV), combined horsepower, combined torque, transmission type, EPA fuel economy rating (city/highway/combined), WLTP range (for EVs), battery capacity (kWh for EVs), and emissions classification. Distinct from engineering powertrain design data — this is the commercial specification layer.

SSOT for the orderable SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) — the fully specified, buildable vehicle configuration combining nameplate, MY, trim level, powertrain, body style, and option packages into a unique orderable unit. Captures SKU code, SKU description, body style, drivetrain type (FWD/RWD/AWD/4WD), engine/powertrain code, transmission type, exterior color code, interior color/material code, market destination code, and SKU lifecycle status. The SKU is the atomic unit used in order management, production scheduling, and dealer inventory.

SSOT for vehicle nameplate definitions — the commercial brand identity of a vehicle line (e.g., F-150, Silverado, Camry, Mustang). Owns nameplate code, brand affiliation, vehicle segment classification (car/truck/SUV/commercial), powertrain family (ICE/HEV/PHEV/EV), market positioning tier, global vs. regional availability flag, nameplate lifecycle status (active/discontinued), SOP (Start of Production) year, EOP (End of Production) year, and nameplate heritage lineage. This is the root anchor for all program and model year planning.

before.description: Defines the annual program plan for each nameplate by MY (Model Year). Captures MY designation, program code, program phase (concept/development/launch/production/runout), SOP date, EOP date, target plant assignments, planned production volume, regulatory homologation targets (CAFE, WLTP, EPA), program budget envelope (CapEx), and program manager reference. Acts as the planning backbone linking nameplate definitions to annual production and sales programs.

Defines commercially available option packages and standalone options that can be ordered on a vehicle (e.g., Technology Package, Tow Package, Panoramic Roof, Premium Audio). Captures package code, package name, package type (group/standalone/accessory), MSRP uplift price, content description, constraint rules (requires/excludes other packages), availability by trim level, market availability regions, and lifecycle status. Distinct from engineering feature definitions — this is the commercial catalog layer.

Defines the commercial trim hierarchy for a model year program (e.g., Base, XL, XLT, Lariat, Platinum, Limited). Captures trim code, trim name, trim rank/order within the nameplate hierarchy, standard feature set description, MSRP base price, market segment positioning, availability regions, and active/inactive lifecycle status. Trim levels are the primary commercial differentiation layer between the nameplate and individual option packages.

Reference catalog of commercial body style definitions available across nameplates (e.g., 2-door coupe, 4-door sedan, crew cab pickup, extended cab, SUV 3-row, cargo van). Captures body style code, body style name, door count, seating capacity, cargo volume, roof type, body structure classification (unibody/body-on-frame), and applicable vehicle segment. Used in SKU construction, order management, and regulatory homologation classification.

Commercial color catalog defining all available exterior paint colors and interior color/material combinations offered across model year programs. Captures color code, color name, color type (exterior/interior), color family, paint technology (solid/metallic/pearl/matte), interior material type (cloth/leather/synthetic/premium), availability by trim level, MSRP uplift (for premium colors), regional availability, and active/discontinued status. Used in SKU configuration, order management, and production scheduling.

Defines market-specific homologation variants of a base SKU required to meet local regulatory standards (UNECE, FMVSS, ADR, etc.). Captures homologation variant code, base SKU reference, target market/country, regulatory standard (UNECE/FMVSS/ADR/CARB), required modification description, homologation approval number, approval authority, approval date, expiry date, and variant status. Bridges the commercial product catalog to the compliance domain's regulatory approval records.
Master reference table for market. Referenced by market_id.

Defines the feature-to-market availability matrix — which SKUs, trim levels, and option packages are available in which geographic markets and sales channels. Captures market code, sales channel (retail/fleet/government/export), availability status (available/restricted/not-offered), launch date, withdrawal date, homologation approval status, import duty classification, and CKD/SKD (Completely Knocked Down / Semi Knocked Down) assembly flag. Critical for order management, dealer ordering systems, and regulatory compliance.

SSOT for MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) price books by model year, market, and currency. Captures price book code, effective date range, market/region code, currency code, price book status (draft/approved/published/superseded), approval authority, and publication date. The price book is the container for all MSRP pricing entries and governs which prices are active for dealer ordering and consumer-facing communications.

Individual MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) pricing entries within a price book. Captures the SKU or option package being priced, base MSRP amount, destination charge, gas guzzler tax (if applicable), effective start and end dates, price type (base vehicle/option/package/accessory), and prior price for change tracking. Enables dealer invoice generation, consumer window sticker production, and competitive pricing analysis.

SSOT for vehicle nameplate definitions — the commercial brand identity of a vehicle line (e.g., F-150, Silverado, Camry, Mustang). Owns nameplate code, brand affiliation, vehicle segment classification (car/truck/SUV/commercial), powertrain family (ICE/HEV/PHEV/EV), market positioning tier, global vs. regional availability flag, nameplate lifecycle status (active/discontinued), SOP (Start of Production) year, EOP (End of Production) year, and nameplate heritage lineage. This is the root anchor for all program and model year planning.

The formal dealer order guide defining which SKUs, trim levels, option packages, and colors are orderable by dealers for a given MY, market, and sales channel. Captures order guide version, effective date range, market/region, sales channel, orderable SKU list, option availability matrix, minimum/maximum order constraints, and order guide approval status. Published to dealer DMS systems and governs what dealers can order from the factory.

Commercial powertrain configuration catalog defining the orderable powertrain combinations available for each nameplate and MY. Captures powertrain code, engine displacement, cylinder count, fuel type (gasoline/diesel/hybrid/PHEV/BEV/FCEV), electric motor configuration (for EV/HEV/PHEV), combined horsepower, combined torque, transmission type, EPA fuel economy rating (city/highway/combined), WLTP range (for EVs), battery capacity (kWh for EVs), and emissions classification. Distinct from engineering powertrain design data — this is the commercial specification layer.

SSOT for the orderable SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) — the fully specified, buildable vehicle configuration combining nameplate, MY, trim level, powertrain, body style, and option packages into a unique orderable unit. Captures SKU code, SKU description, body style, drivetrain type (FWD/RWD/AWD/4WD), engine/powertrain code, transmission type, exterior color code, interior color/material code, market destination code, and SKU lifecycle status. The SKU is the atomic unit used in order management, production scheduling, and dealer inventory.

after.description: Defines the annual program plan for each nameplate by MY (Model Year). Captures MY designation, program code, program phase (concept/development/launch/production/runout), SOP date, EOP date, target plant assignments, planned production volume, regulatory homologation targets (CAFE, WLTP, EPA), program budget envelope (CapEx), and program manager reference. Acts as the planning backbone linking nameplate definitions to annual production and sales programs.

Defines commercially available option packages and standalone options that can be ordered on a vehicle (e.g., Technology Package, Tow Package, Panoramic Roof, Premium Audio). Captures package code, package name, package type (group/standalone/accessory), MSRP uplift price, content description, constraint rules (requires/excludes other packages), availability by trim level, market availability regions, and lifecycle status. Distinct from engineering feature definitions — this is the commercial catalog layer.

Defines the commercial trim hierarchy for a model year program (e.g., Base, XL, XLT, Lariat, Platinum, Limited). Captures trim code, trim name, trim rank/order within the nameplate hierarchy, standard feature set description, MSRP base price, market segment positioning, availability regions, and active/inactive lifecycle status. Trim levels are the primary commercial differentiation layer between the nameplate and individual option packages.

Defines the feature-to-market availability matrix — which SKUs, trim levels, and option packages are available in which geographic markets and sales channels. Captures market code, sales channel (retail/fleet/government/export), availability status (available/restricted/not-offered), launch date, withdrawal date, homologation approval status, import duty classification, and CKD/SKD (Completely Knocked Down / Semi Knocked Down) assembly flag. Critical for order management, dealer ordering systems, and regulatory compliance.

SSOT for MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) price books by model year, market, and currency. Captures price book code, effective date range, market/region code, currency code, price book status (draft/approved/published/superseded), approval authority, and publication date. The price book is the container for all MSRP pricing entries and governs which prices are active for dealer ordering and consumer-facing communications.

Individual MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) pricing entries within a price book. Captures the SKU or option package being priced, base MSRP amount, destination charge, gas guzzler tax (if applicable), effective start and end dates, price type (base vehicle/option/package/accessory), and prior price for change tracking. Enables dealer invoice generation, consumer window sticker production, and competitive pricing analysis.

The formal dealer order guide defining which SKUs, trim levels, option packages, and colors are orderable by dealers for a given MY, market, and sales channel. Captures order guide version, effective date range, market/region, sales channel, orderable SKU list, option availability matrix, minimum/maximum order constraints, and order guide approval status. Published to dealer DMS systems and governs what dealers can order from the factory.

SSOT for the orderable SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) — the fully specified, buildable vehicle configuration combining nameplate, MY, trim level, powertrain, body style, and option packages into a unique orderable unit. Captures SKU code, SKU description, body style, drivetrain type (FWD/RWD/AWD/4WD), engine/powertrain code, transmission type, exterior color code, interior color/material code, market destination code, and SKU lifecycle status. The SKU is the atomic unit used in order management, production scheduling, and dealer inventory.
Cumulative number of units actually produced to date for this model year program. Updated as production progresses.
SAE automation level for ADAS features included in this model year program. Level 0: no automation; Level 5: full automation.

The percentage of the product value that is sourced or manufactured locally in the target market. Used for trade agreement compliance and preferential duty qualification.
Unique identifier for the market availability record. Primary key for the market availability entity.
The geographic market or country code where this product configuration is available for sale. Uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country codes.

The duration of the manufacturer's powertrain warranty coverage (engine, transmission, drivetrain) for this product configuration in the target market, expressed in months. Typically longer than basic warranty.

lineage.vibe: Rename product aftersales.nameplate to aftersales_nameplate because 'nameplate' is a generic name that conflicts with the product domain's SSOT responsibility, and it should be prefixed for clarity since it is heavily referenced.
Rename product aftersales.body_style to aftersales_body_style because the bare name 'body_style' reads as a lookup belonging in vehicle/product domain and needs disambiguation.
Rename product aftersales.color_option to aftersales_color_option because the bare name conflicts with vehicle domain responsibility and needs domain context.
Rename product aftersales.market to aftersales_market because the bare name 'market' is ambiguous and could be confused with sales territory or compliance jurisdiction.
Move product aftersales.nameplate to the product domain because nameplate definitions are explicitly the product domain SSOT responsibility.
Move product aftersales.body_style to the vehicle domain because body style is a vehicle master data attribute, not an aftersales concept.
Move product aftersales.color_option to the vehicle domain because color options are vehicle configuration attributes, not aftersales-specific.
Move product aftersales.sku to the product domain because SKU structures are explicitly listed as product domain SSOT responsibility.
Move product aftersales.aftersales_trim_level to the product domain because trim level definitions belong in the commercial product catalog, not aftersales.
Move product aftersales.aftersales_option_package to the product domain because option/package configurations are explicitly product domain SSOT.
Move product aftersales.aftersales_model_year_program to the product domain because model year program plans are explicitly product domain SSOT.
Move product aftersales.msrp_price_book to the product domain because MSRP price books are explicitly listed as product domain SSOT responsibility.
Move product aftersales.msrp_price_entry to the product domain because MSRP pricing entries belong with the price book in the product domain.
Move product aftersales.market_availability to the product domain because feature-to-market availability matrices are explicitly product domain SSOT.
Move product aftersales.order_guide to the product domain because order guides are product catalog artifacts.
Move product aftersales.powertrain_config to the vehicle domain because powertrain configurations are vehicle master data.
Move product aftersales.homologation_variant to the compliance domain because homologation variants relate to regulatory type approvals.

before.description: Batch billing run record representing a scheduled or ad-hoc execution of the invoice generation process for a defined set of billing accounts, order types, or billing dates. Captures run ID, run type (periodic/manual/correction), billing date, billing category (vehicle_sales/parts/service/fleet/export), number of invoices generated, total billed amount, run status (scheduled/in_progress/completed/failed/cancelled), error count, run initiated by, and SAP SD billing due list execution reference (VF04). Provides operational traceability for mass billing cycles.
Actual date and time when the billing run execution completed or failed, used for duration calculation and operational reporting.
Actual date and time when the billing run execution began, used for performance monitoring and variance analysis against scheduled time.
User ID of the supervisor or manager who approved the billing run for execution, required for high-value or correction runs.
SAP batch job ID or scheduler job reference for the billing run execution, used for technical troubleshooting and job monitoring.

Business classification of the billing scope: vehicle_sales (retail and dealer vehicle invoices), parts (OEM parts and accessories), service (after-sales maintenance and repair), fleet (corporate fleet accounts), export (international sales), warranty (warranty claim reimbursements), lease (leasing contracts), or rental (vehicle rental charges). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: vehicle_sales|parts|service|fleet|export|warranty|lease|rental — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The business date on which invoices in this run are dated and become effective for accounting and payment terms calculation. Determines invoice due dates and fiscal period assignment.
SAP SD transaction VF04 billing due list execution reference number, linking this run to the SAP billing due list selection and processing log.
Code identifying the legal entity or company code issuing the invoices in this run, used for multi-entity OEM structures and regional billing organizations.
End date of the billing period covered by this run, defining the cutoff for transactions included in the batch.
Foreign key linking to billing.billing_period. Business justification: A billing run belongs to a billing period; linking run to billing_period clarifies the period context.
Start date of the billing period covered by this run, used for periodic billing cycles (e.g., monthly vehicle sales, service contracts).
Timestamp when the billing run record was first created in the system, used for audit trail and data lineage.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the total billed amount (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY), representing the reporting currency for this run.
SAP SD distribution channel code for the billing run (e.g., dealer network, direct sales, online, fleet).
SAP SD division code representing the product line or business segment (e.g., passenger vehicles, commercial trucks, parts, service).

Status of EDI 810 invoice transmission for this billing run: not_applicable (no EDI invoices), pending (queued), transmitted (sent to trading partners), acknowledged (receipt confirmed), or failed (transmission error).
User ID or system account that triggered the billing run, used for audit trail and accountability.
Total number of errors encountered during the billing run execution, including validation errors, data quality issues, and system exceptions.
Fiscal period (month or quarter) within the fiscal year to which the billing run is assigned, used for period-based revenue reporting.
Fiscal year to which the billing run and generated invoices are assigned for financial reporting and period closing.
Free-text notes and comments about the billing run execution, including special instructions, known issues, or manual interventions performed.
Primary output format for invoices generated in this run: pdf (electronic document), xml (structured data), edi (EDI 810 invoice), print (physical mail), or email (direct delivery).
Date on which the billing run invoices are posted to the financial ledger in SAP FI, determining the accounting period for revenue recognition.
Name of the SAP output device or print queue to which invoices were sent for physical printing and mailing.
Date on which the billing run was reversed and credit memos were issued to cancel the original invoices.
Indicates whether this billing run was subsequently reversed or cancelled, requiring credit memo generation and financial adjustment.
Code indicating the reason for billing run reversal (e.g., pricing error, wrong billing date, duplicate run, system error).
User ID of the supervisor or manager who approved the billing run for execution, required for high-value or correction runs.
User ID or system account that triggered the billing run, used for audit trail and accountability.
Unique identifier for the billing run batch execution. Primary key.
Human-readable business identifier for the billing run, typically formatted as BR-YYYYMMDD-NNNN for traceability and audit purposes.

Current lifecycle state of the billing run: scheduled (queued for execution), in_progress (actively processing), completed (successfully finished), failed (terminated with errors), cancelled (aborted by user), or partially_completed (finished with some errors).

Classification of the billing run execution mode: periodic (scheduled recurring), manual (user-initiated), correction (error fix), rerun (retry after failure), ad_hoc (one-time special), or final (end-of-period closing).
SAP SD sales organization responsible for the billing run, representing the commercial unit (e.g., North America Automotive, Europe Commercial Vehicles).
Planned date and time when the billing run was scheduled to begin execution, used for batch job planning and SLA tracking.
Business rules and filters applied to select billing-eligible documents for this run (e.g., customer group, sales order type, delivery date range, billing block status).
Sum of all net invoice amounts generated in this billing run, representing the total revenue recognized in the batch.
Sum of all discounts, rebates, and allowances applied across invoices in this run, used for pricing analytics and margin analysis.
Sum of all gross invoice amounts before discounts and taxes across all invoices in this run, representing the list-price revenue.
Number of invoice generation attempts that failed due to data errors, validation failures, or system issues during this run.
Total number of invoice documents successfully created during this billing run, used for volume tracking and reconciliation.
Sum of all tax amounts (VAT, sales tax, GST) across all invoices generated in this run, used for tax reporting and reconciliation.
Timestamp when the billing run record was last modified, capturing status changes, error updates, and completion events.
Total number of warnings generated during the billing run, indicating non-critical issues that did not prevent invoice creation but require review.

before.description: Record of a billing block applied to a sales order, delivery, or billing account that prevents invoice generation until the block is resolved. Captures block type (credit_limit_exceeded/pricing_incomplete/legal_hold/compliance_hold/dispute_hold/manual_hold), blocked document reference, block applied date, block applied by, block reason description, release date, released by, and SAP SD billing block code reference. Supports credit management and compliance-driven invoice holds.
Foreign key linking to billing.account. Business justification: Blocks can be applied at the account level; adding account_id creates a direct relationship and removes no redundant columns.
Number of days the billing block has been active since application, used for aging analysis and escalation triggers.
Full name of the user who applied the billing block, for business user reference and audit purposes.
Date on which the billing block was applied to the document, preventing invoice generation.
Precise timestamp when the billing block was applied, including time-of-day for audit and tracking purposes.
User ID or system identifier of the person or automated process that applied the billing block.
Unique identifier for the billing block record. Primary key.
Business-facing unique identifier or reference number for the billing block, used for tracking and communication purposes.
User ID or system identifier of the person or automated process that released the billing block.
Current lifecycle status of the billing block. Active blocks prevent invoicing; released blocks have been cleared.
Category of billing block applied. Indicates the reason category for preventing invoice generation.
Reference number of the sales order, delivery, or billing account that is blocked from invoicing.
Type of document to which the billing block is applied (e.g., sales order, delivery, billing account).
SAP company code representing the legal entity to which the blocked billing document belongs.
Specific compliance or regulatory reason for the billing hold, such as export control, sanctions screening, or regulatory investigation.
Timestamp when this billing block record was first created in the system, for audit trail and data lineage purposes.
Total credit exposure amount for the customer at the time the billing block was applied, used in credit limit evaluation.
Approved credit limit for the customer at the time of billing block application, used for credit hold decisions.
Indicates whether the billing block was triggered due to the customer exceeding their approved credit limit.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for credit exposure and limit amounts.
Identifier of the customer account associated with the blocked billing document.
Identifier of the dealer associated with the blocked billing document, if applicable to dealer transactions.
Identifier of the dealer associated with the blocked billing document, if applicable to dealer transactions.
Delivery document number associated with the billing block, if the block is applied at the delivery level.
Identifier of the customer dispute record associated with this billing block, if the block is dispute-related.
SAP distribution channel through which the blocked billing document was processed (e.g., retail, fleet, wholesale).
SAP division or product line associated with the blocked billing document (e.g., passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, parts).

Date on which the billing block was escalated for higher-level review or resolution.
Indicates whether the billing block has been escalated to management or a specialized resolution team due to age or complexity.
Target date by which the billing block is expected to be resolved and released, used for SLA tracking and customer communication.
Fiscal period (month or quarter) within the fiscal year when the billing block was applied.
Fiscal year in which the billing block was applied, used for financial period reporting and analysis.
Case or matter number for legal holds, linking the billing block to a specific legal proceeding or investigation.
General free-text notes or comments related to the billing block, capturing additional context, communications, or resolution actions.
Identifier of the customer account associated with the blocked billing document.
Priority level assigned to the billing block for resolution workflow and escalation management.
Standardized code representing the specific reason for the billing block. Maps to SAP SD billing block reason master data.

Create the field_services domain with the following products: field_technician_dispatch, mobile_service_order, roadside_assistance_case, towing_event, breakdown_case, field_visit, field_activity, field_quality_investigation, field_failure_analysis, field_engineering_report, field_service_appointment, field_parts_usage.
